item.title: Backup & restore
item.description: Backup & restore The plugin doesn’t run its own backup.

item.title: Migrating between hosts
item.description: Migrating between hosts Move your vault from one remote host to another (Pi → NAS, home server → VPS, old hardware → new) with no edit gap and no surprises.

item.title: Cookbook
item.description: Cookbook Goal-oriented walkthroughs that compose pieces from the rest of these docs. If you want a step-by-step “how do I…” answer, start here.

item.title: Architecture
item.description: Architecture Design specs for the major subsystems — the why behind decisions, not just the what of the code.

item.title: First connect
item.description: First connect — what’s actually happening The shadow vault model obsidian-remote-ssh does not edit your remote files directly through Obsidian’s vault layer.

item.title: Reconnect behavior
item.description: Reconnect behavior When the SSH connection drops mid-session, the plugin retries up to 5 times with ×1.5 exponential backoff (1 s → 1.5 s → 2.25 s → … capped at 30 s) before surfacing an error.

item.title: Token & socket
item.description: Token & socket The daemon authenticates clients via a 32-byte shared-secret token written to a 0600-mode file at startup, never persisted across daemon restarts.

item.title: Binary signing
item.description: Binary signing Every release binary is signed with Cosign keyless (Sigstore OIDC) by the GitHub Actions workflow that produced it — no GPG key management, no trust roots to bootstrap.

item.title: Host keys & trust
item.description: Host keys & trust obsidian-remote-ssh maintains its own known-host store (separate from ~/.ssh/known_hosts) so trust stays scoped to the plugin.

item.title: Jump hosts (bastions)
item.description: Jump hosts (bastions) When the host you want to edit is not directly reachable — it sits behind a bastion / corporate gateway / Tailscale exit node — obsidian-remote-ssh can chain through one or more jump hosts (ssh -J-style).
